todays_decisions.reasoning: I agree with the Market Analyst's neutral stance: SPY is 5.7% above its 200-day, but tech and communication are rolling over, defensives lead, and the Fed decision (10-28) plus three mega-cap reports land this week. The account is about 85% invested with 14.7% cash, so idle cash does count against us, but neither proposal has a strong enough edge to justify full size into the event. MSM is a clean, event-clear, 9/9 F-score name with low beta (0.72), so I keep it but halve it because the Skeptic and Implicator are right that it is an industrial-distribution peer of FAST (same MRO theme, not a new sector) and the Market Analyst says to avoid Industrials. VXUS is rejected for now: it is below its 200-day, has a beta of 1.11 (it would not cushion a drawdown), emerging-market stress (EWZ -21%, China AI rout) is still unfolding, and the proposer concedes it is not a conviction call, so nothing is lost by waiting a day for the Fed. Lesson L1 shaped the MSM stop: it is anchored to the actual fill, not the stale 10-22 menu close, because the post-print price reaction is unknown. L2 was satisfied for MSM (8-K 2.02 and 10-K filed 10-22, next earnings about 2027-01-06). Cash after this trade is roughly 13%, which leaves room to add diversification (VXUS or similar) after the Fed if the trend holds.

trades.thesis: Quality industrial distributor: 9/9 F-score, cash flow $306M vs net income $223M, newest 10-K on the menu, already reported on 10-22 so no earnings event in the window, low beta (0.72). Sized small (about 1.3% of equity) because it overlaps FAST's industrial-MRO exposure, profitability (gp 0.65) is the weakest on the analyst's list, and the Market Analyst tilts away from Industrials.
trades.invalidation: Close more than about 9% below the actual fill price (re-anchor to the fill, not the $118.72 menu close; roughly $108 only if it fills near the menu close), or a new 8-K showing a guidance cut or restatement of the FY2026 results.

rejected.why: The Skeptic's case is stronger than the proposal. VXUS is already below its 200-day (-0.41%) and the Market Analyst prefers broad US exposure over international, which we already hold through VOO and VTI. The Implicator confirms it has a beta of 1.11, higher than VOO and VTI, so it diversifies geography but not drawdown risk, and the Brazil and China rout is still unfolding. The proposer calls it not a conviction call, and the invalidation level is inconsistent (80.0 is about 3.6% below the 200-day, not 3%). With the Fed decision tomorrow there is no cost to waiting for a post-meeting close above the 200-day before adding non-US exposure.

DPZ.thesis: High-quality, cash-backed franchisor (F-score 8/9, cfo $792M vs net income $602M, gross profitability 1.15) with a 252d beta of 0.095 (-$0.62 on this position in a 10% market drop). That makes it a genuinely defensive starter position while the tape rotates away from tech. Its top-of-sector rank is partly an artifact of the wholesale-groceries mislabel, so the case rests on its absolute quality and low beta, not on the Staples tilt. No earnings inside 5 trading days.
DPZ.invalidation: DPZ closes below $274.88 (10% under the $305.42 reference close), or a fundamentals screen (including one that reflects the Q3 results reported 10-13) drops it from the menu or shows cfo below net income.

IDXX.thesis: Quality Health Care name in a favored sector (F-score 8/9, gp_sector_pct 0.941, cfo $1,182M vs net income $1,059M, no added leverage or dilution). Sized down to $40 because its 0.814 beta (-$3.26 on this position in a 10% drop) makes it the least defensive holding in the book. Earnings are estimated for 11-02, outside the 5-day window.
IDXX.invalidation: IDXX closes below $500.22 (10% under the $555.80 reference close), or IDXX underperforms XLV by more than 5 percentage points over a 21-trading-day window.

VOO.thesis: Regime filter is on (SPY +4.97% over its 200-day) and broad US equity is the acceptable core sleeve while QQQ and international are the risky ones. Sized down from $15 to leave headroom under the 15% position cap, as the Skeptic and Implicator both note, and to avoid adding full beta into the Fed and earnings week.
VOO.invalidation: SPY closes below its 200-day average (723.99), which also turns the code regime filter off, or RSP turns negative on the 21-day return, showing the correction is broadening.

WMT.thesis: Low-volatility defensive exposure (vol 0.263, beta about zero; not a hedge) in a favored sector (XLP +6.02% 21d), with positive sell-side sentiment and no earnings until ~11-19. Fundamentals pass the screen (F-score 7, gp_sector_pct 0.865) with no red flags. Sized below the proposal because the staples move has already run and today's upgrades may be priced in, and because it lifts the Consumer Staples label to about 22.5% of equity alongside DPZ.
WMT.invalidation: WMT closes more than 7% below entry, or XLP gives back half its 21-day gain (21-day return below ~+3%) while SPY holds, or WMT cuts guidance at its ~11-19 report.

VTI.thesis: Broad-market exposure to deploy idle cash while the trend is intact and breadth is improving. The Skeptic and Implicator note it largely duplicates VOO and raises beta, and that small caps are weak, so I buy a smaller tranche and hold back the rest given the risk-off open. Resulting US broad-ETF weight is about 18.4%.
VTI.invalidation: SPY closes below its 200-day SMA (723.23), or the position is down more than 8% from the actual fill.

FAST.thesis: Lowest volatility on the menu (0.243), F-score 8/9, gross profitability at the 89th sector percentile, and operating cash flow above net income. It adds a first Consumer Discretionary exposure, not overlapping the staples names held. Resized from $40: the Skeptic is right that its earnings date was never verified, that cash conversion is only about 1.03x, and that the sector label may flatter it. The Implicator confirmed the diversification claim holds.
FAST.invalidation: A close more than 10% below the actual fill price, or an earnings report showing operating cash flow clearly below net income.

CARG.thesis: Rank 2 on fundamentals (gross profitability 1.27, cfo about 2x net income), earnings 11-05 are outside the 5-day window, and no adverse headlines. The Skeptic's objections (averaging a one-day-old position, Technology label against the sector view, vol near the cutoff) justify a small add: the combined position is about 5%, and I will judge it as one position.
CARG.invalidation: Combined position closes more than 10% below the average fill (measured from actual fills, per L1), or a negative earnings surprise appears inside the next five trading days.

BTC/USD.thesis: A small crypto slot: trend still positive (63-day +28%, 14% above its 200-day), ETF inflows recovering, and no exchange failures or new adverse regulatory action. Resized from $20: the Skeptic is right that the thesis is mostly diversification, volatility is 44%, and the recovery partly rides on the same Iran-deal headline as energy. The Implicator's stress test shows this is the highest-risk sleeve per dollar.
BTC/USD.invalidation: A close more than 10% below the actual fill price, or an exchange failure or adverse regulatory action appears in the news.

KR.thesis: Staples is a Market Analyst favored sector, KR has low event risk (next earnings 12-03, the 10-20 8-K was an investor-day update) and the sell side is supportive after the 7-11% EPS CAGR target. The Skeptic and Implicator are right that this stacks on WMT and DPZ (staples about 22.5% of equity) and that the negative beta is a statistical artifact, so I take a smaller position, which lifts staples only to about 25.9%.
KR.invalidation: Close more than 8% below the actual fill price, or the 10-17 grocery-chain cyber incident is confirmed to be Kroger, or a guidance cut at the 12-03 print.

MSCI.thesis: Clean Q3 beat with the earnings event passed (the issue that sank it on 10-20), F-score 8, cfo $1.59B vs net income $1.20B, beta 0.34, and it adds a sector the book does not hold. The Skeptic is right that the sector label is Industrials (not a favored sector) and that the post-print re-rating is partly priced, so I trim the size and rest the case on quality and diversification only.
MSCI.invalidation: Close more than 8% below the actual fill price (anchored to the fill, not the pre-print 563.49 close, per L1), or a guidance cut or negative 8-K follow-up.

VRSN.thesis: Top-ranked quality name (9/9 F-score, cash flow well above net income). Q3 was reported on 10-22 and the next estimate is 2027-02-04, so there is no earnings event ahead. Beta is about 0.02, so it adds almost no market risk. Sized down from $15 because the Skeptic is right that the add chases a 3.6% gain, and the fundamentals data predates the Q3 print.
VRSN.invalidation: VRSN closes below 278, about 8% under the expected fill near $303 (anchored to the fill per L1, not the $292.23 first lot), or a later filing shows the guide raise was reversed.

BND.thesis: The account holds no bonds and bonds are the one sleeve rallying (+1.13% over 21 days, 4% vol). BND diversifies against the equity-heavy book and the tech sell-off. It is not a short-duration fund, and the rally is reversible around next week's Fed meeting, so it is held as the only bond holding at a modest size. The Skeptic's duplicate objection is met by rejecting IEF.
BND.invalidation: Sell if BND closes more than 2% below the fill price, or if a hawkish Fed pushes the 10-year back above 5.15%.

IEF.thesis: Tactical Treasury add: IEF 21d +1.87% at low volatility, preferred over TLT by the Market Analyst, and it diversifies a book that is mostly equities with only BND as a bond sleeve. Sized down from $20 because the Skeptic is right that the Fed decision this week is two-way duration risk and that IEF is still below its 200-day.
IEF.invalidation: IEF closes below 89.5 (about 1.7% under the 91.05 reference, re-checked against the actual fill), or a hawkish Fed outcome pushes yields materially higher.

MSM.thesis: Quality industrial distributor: 9/9 F-score, cash flow $306M vs net income $223M, newest 10-K on the menu, already reported on 10-22 so no earnings event in the window, low beta (0.72). Sized small (about 1.3% of equity) because it overlaps FAST's industrial-MRO exposure, profitability (gp 0.65) is the weakest on the analyst's list, and the Market Analyst tilts away from Industrials.
MSM.invalidation: Close more than about 9% below the actual fill price (re-anchor to the fill, not the $118.72 menu close; roughly $108 only if it fills near the menu close), or a new 8-K showing a guidance cut or restatement of the FY2026 results.
